title: Viewport Edit
summary: Edit buttons where you see them: pick one on the item, add one, rearrange the row, and remove a menu you don't need.

steps.title: Step 1: Pick a Button on the Item
text: 1. At the top of the Kneady tab, click Viewport Edit.
2. Click Nod on the mannequin's head.

Nod's row is selected in the tree, under Head, and its settings show below it. In Viewport Edit a click on a button still does what it does - a toggle switches, a menu opens - and selects it too. Ctrl+click only selects it, and a click on a region's faces selects the region.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the head

steps.title: Step 2: Add a Button
text: 1. Hover the head: icons sit out from the corners of the square round its buttons.
2. Click + at the top right. A new button joins the row, selected.
3. Double-click its name in the tree (or Ctrl+click it), type Tilt and press Enter.
+ adds to the buttons showing - the row, or the menu that's open. Tilt drives nothing yet: Copy and Reuse, next, gives it Turn's commands.

media.label: By the head, then in the tree

steps.title: Step 3: Rearrange the Row
text: 1. Hover the head and click the grip of six dots at the top left. It turns blue: Rearrange is on.
2. Drag Tilt between Nod and Turn, and let go.
3. Click the grip again to turn Rearrange off.
While Rearrange is on, a drag picks a button up instead of running it, and the others make room as it passes. The order is the tree's: Tilt is second there too.

steps.title: Step 4: Remove a Menu
text: 1. Hover the chest. Spare is a menu left from an earlier layout, and nothing in it drives anything.
2. Ctrl+click Spare: it is selected, and its menu stays closed.

A click would have opened Spare's menu; Ctrl+click selects a button without doing what it does. - removes the button selected, and the buttons in its menu go with it, so Kneady asks first. Click Viewport Edit again when you're done.
